position: Office of Air and Radiation: Regulating Hydrofluorocarbons Under the AIM Act
proposal: The Mandate recommends repealing Biden-era regulations implementing the AIM Act that are unnecessarily stringent and costly, and declining petitions from manufacturers to add restrictions that push the market toward costlier refrigerants and equipment. status_summary: A final rule published 2026-05-26 and effective 2026-07-27 relaxes parts of the 2023 Technology Transitions restrictions: it sets interim global warming potential limits for supermarket systems, remote condensing units and cold storage warehouses that run until 2032, delays some compliance dates, and removes the installation deadline for residential and light commercial air conditioning and heat pump equipment whose components were made or imported before 2025. EPA estimated engineering cost savings with a present value of about 976 million dollars at a 3 percent discount rate (2026 to 2050). A proposal of the same date would exempt road and intermodal transport refrigeration units from the leak repair requirements. Petitions for review of the final rule were filed in the D.C. Circuit by industry groups on 2026-06-25, by an environmental group on 2026-07-20 and by 18 states, the District of Columbia and the City of New York in a petition signed 2026-07-21, with no stay or ruling found. The statutory HFC phasedown remains in place, and on 2026-07-28 EPA released allocation data ahead of a planned rulemaking that will seek comment on allowances starting in 2029.
